findings.claim: Duplicate keys now pass silently. A [MessagePackObject] with two members sharing [Key(0)] (or the same string key) previously made `intMembers.Add` / `stringMembers.Add` throw. That surfaced as AD0001/CS8785, so the problem was visible. The new `ContainsKey` guard keeps the first member and drops the second without reporting anything. With no diagnostic, the analyzer stops flagging a type that the dynamic resolver rejects at run time ('key is duplicated'). For types that are not suppressed, the generated formatter silently omits the second member, so its data is lost on round-trip.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.DuplicateKeyDiagnosticTests. It compiles `[MessagePackObject] public class Dup { [Key(0)] public int A {get;set;} [Key(0)] public int B {get;set;} }` (plain and with SuppressSourceGeneration = true) and runs every DiagnosticAnalyzer in the MessagePack.SourceGenerator assembly. It asserts that at least one Error-severity MsgPack diagnostic is reported. On head none is expected, so the test fails. The same applies to the string-key guard at line 1039 and the copies at lines 1163 and 1179.
